page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.6xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance within the ecs.c7se Enhanced family, running on KVM hypervisor architecture. Powered by a dedicated 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor, it features 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system incorporates 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache per core. Memory capacity is 48.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware instruction capabilities include AVX-512 with VNNI extensions, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA. The instance lacks local disk storage and relies on network-attached storage, while providing an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates middle-tier performance across standard compute and memory workloads. PassMark CPU score reaches 29295.6, while Geekbench multi-core and single-core scores stand at 12129.0 and 1596.0 respectively. Stress-ng records multi-core CPU performance at 23294.91. Memory bandwidth reaches 129.22 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 63.67 GB/sec for large writes. In small language model evaluations (135M model), it achieves 293.82 tokens per second for text generation, while prompt processing reaches 1822.75 tokens per second. Redis SET throughput measures 23.8 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 27.97 GB/sec.

With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.c7se.6xlarge offers resource density tailored for compute-focused tasks that do not require high memory footprints. The absence of local disk storage requires allocation of network storage over its 8 Gbps interface. This hardware combination is suitable for CPU-bound batch jobs, software compilation, microservices hosting, web serving, and small-model inference tasks.
